n: The Lord calls the distant nations into a courtroom: be quiet, gather your strength, then come and argue your case. The trial will show who is truly God.

f.g: Coastlands—distant nations, especially in the west.

f.w: let us come near together to judgment

n: Who stirred up a conqueror from the east who crushes kings like dust? Most readers see Cyrus of Persia, named in Isaiah 44:28–45:1, who conquered Babylon in 539 BC.

f.w: the righteous man from the east
f.g: Or “one whom righteousness calls”; often identified with Cyrus the Great.

f.w: as driven stubble to his bow

n: The conqueror moves so fast he hardly seems to touch the ground, passing safely through unfamiliar territory.
The answer: the Lord did it. He is “the first, and with the last”—present from the beginning to the end of history. Latter-day Saints recognize Jesus Christ as Jehovah, the First and the Last.

f.w: the first, and with the last

n: The far-off nations tremble at the conqueror’s rise and huddle together in fear.
Their response is to encourage one another—not to turn to God, but to make more idols.
Isaiah mocks the scene: craftsmen cheer each other on, solder the idol, and nail it down so it won’t tip over. They trust a god they have to fasten in place.

f.w: that it should not be moved

n: In contrast, Israel is God’s servant, chosen, descended from Abraham, whom God called His friend. Israel’s identity rests on God’s covenant, not on idols.
God reminds Israel that He called Abraham from a far country and chose his family—and He has not thrown them away, even in exile.

f.w: I have chosen thee, and not cast thee away

n: One of scripture’s most comforting verses: don’t be afraid, I am with you; I am your God; I will strengthen, help, and hold you up with My righteous right hand.

f.w: Fear thou not; for I am with thee
the right hand of my righteousness
f.g: The right hand symbolizes power and covenant faithfulness.

n: Those who rage against Israel will end up ashamed; those who fight against them will disappear.
Israel will look for their enemies and not even find them—they will have vanished.
The Lord takes Israel by the right hand, like a parent holding a child’s hand, and repeats: don’t fear, I will help you.

f.w: I the LORD thy God will hold thy right hand

n: Israel is small and weak as a worm, yet the Holy One is their Redeemer—the kinsman who buys back a relative from slavery. Christ is the great Redeemer.

f.g: A picture of helplessness, not contempt.
Hebrew go’el—the near relative who rescues or buys back family members.

n: The weak worm becomes a powerful threshing sledge with sharp teeth that grinds mountains to dust. God will turn weakness into strength.

f.g: A heavy board studded with stones or iron, dragged over grain to break it.

n: Like winnowed chaff, the obstacles blow away, and Israel rejoices in the Lord—giving Him, not themselves, the credit.

f.g: Winnow—toss grain in the air so the wind blows away chaff.

n: When the poor and thirsty search for water and find none, the Lord will answer them. He never abandons the needy.

f.w: I the LORD will hear them

n: God will make rivers flow on bare hills and springs in dry valleys—a new Exodus with miraculous water in the desert.

f.w: I will make the wilderness a pool of water

n: He will plant a forest of fine trees in the desert. The barren land blooms—a symbol of the restoration of His people.

f.g: The acacia, whose wood was used for the tabernacle.
Probably a cypress or similar evergreen.

n: The purpose: so everyone will see and understand that the Lord’s hand did it. Restoration testifies of God.
Back in court, the Lord challenges the idols: present your case and your best arguments.

f.g: A title of the Lord as Israel’s true king.

n: The test: let the idols explain the past or predict the future. A true God knows history from beginning to end.

f.w: declare us things for to come

n: Do anything at all—good or bad—just prove you are real! The idols are silent.
The verdict: the idols are nothing, and choosing them is detestable.
God again speaks of the conqueror He has raised—coming from the north and the east (Persia lay east, and its armies came down from the north). He will trample rulers like a potter treads clay.

f.w: from the rising of the sun
shall he call upon my name

n: Which idol announced this ahead of time so we could say it was right? None.
The Lord was first to announce good news to Zion and give Jerusalem a herald of hope.
God looked among the idols and their worshippers for anyone to answer, but no one could say a word.
Final judgment: the idols are empty, their works worthless, their metal images just wind.
